chunks: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) regarding the supplication 'Praise is for Allah, the end-point of His knowledge.'
So he wrote back to me: Do not say 'end-point of His knowledge', for His knowledge has no end-point. Rather, say 'end-point of His pleasure.'

key_terms.رِضَاهُ: His pleasure, satisfaction, or approval — referring to God's contentment with righteous acts
key_terms.عِلْمِهِ: His knowledge — referring to God's omniscience
key_terms.مُنْتَهَى: End-point, ultimate limit, the farthest extent of something

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Ridha correct the phrase 'end-point of His knowledge' in a supplication?
ai.summary: In this hadith, al-Kahili inquires of Imam Abu al-Hasan (likely Imam al-Ridha) about a phrase he was using in a supplication that described God's knowledge as having an 'end-point.' The Imam corrects this formulation, clarifying that God's knowledge is infinite and boundless, and therefore cannot be bounded by any expression. Instead, the supplicant should use 'end-point of His pleasure,' since God's pleasure — unlike His knowledge — can be understood as reaching completion through righteous deeds. This reflects the early Shia theological emphasis on proper description of divine attributes, particularly the infinite nature of divine knowledge (al-'ilm al-ilahi).

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Al Kahily who said, 
‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> regarding the supplication ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the end-point of His<sup>azwj</sup> Knowledge’ (دُعَاءٍ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ مُنْتَهَى عِلْمِهِ).

So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote back: ‘Do not be saying, ‘End-point of His<sup>azwj</sup> Knowledge’, for there is no end-point to His<sup>azwj</sup> Knowledge. But, say, ‘End-point of His<sup>azwj</sup> Pleasure (for His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-Kahili who has said the following. “I wrote to abu al-Hassan (al-Kazim) (a.s.), praising Allah in my letter as, ‘All praise belongs to Allah to the limit of His knowledge.’”
He wrote back to me, “Do not say, “To the limit of His knowledge because there is no limit to His knowledge. Instead say, “All praise belongs to Allah to the limit of His pleasure.”
